title: What If a Disease Vanished Without a Vaccine? Guinea Worm Nearly Did

scenes.text: What if a disease could be wiped out with no vaccine and no drug? One nearly was.
In 1986, guinea worm infected about 3.5 million people a year across 21 countries. Each worm grows to about a meter inside the body.
People caught it from drinking water holding tiny infected water fleas. About a year later the worm pushed out through the skin.
There was no cure to give. So villages learned to filter water through cloth and keep infected people out of the pond.
The Carter Center led the push. Cases fell by more than 99.99 percent, and only ten human cases were reported in 2025.
If it ends, guinea worm will be only the second human disease ever eradicated after smallpox, and the first without a vaccine.

description:
What if a disease could be wiped out with no vaccine and no drug?
In 1986 guinea worm infected an estimated 3.5 million people a year in 21 countries. There is no vaccine and no cure; instead, villages learned to filter drinking water and keep infected people away from ponds, with the Carter Center leading the campaign. Human cases fell to a record low of ten in 2025, though infections in animals, mainly dogs in Chad, still make the last steps hard.
What should we run through next?
first_comment: Dogs in Chad are now the last big hurdle. Which disease do you think we should try to wipe out next?
